question: Should this RFC establish `gateway.restore.status` as a new Gateway Protocol contract now, or keep restore observability as a future owner-reviewed seam while the host lifecycle design is validated?
rationale: The proposed method creates a durable public compatibility commitment; source review cannot determine whether maintainers want that API, an alternative surface, or no core surface at this stage.

options.title: Defer the public method
options.body: Keep the ownership split and sidecar rationale, but mark `gateway.restore.status` as non-normative until the Gateway protocol owner approves a concrete API.

options.title: Approve the protocol direction
options.body: Accept the method as a Gateway Protocol commitment and require explicit compatibility, authorization, and operation-identity rules before implementation promotion.

options.title: Keep lifecycle work host-only
options.body: Retain RFC 0013 as the SQLite artifact contract and leave lifecycle inspection entirely to host-private orchestration for now.

recommendation.title: Defer the public method
recommendation.body: Keep the ownership split and sidecar rationale, but mark `gateway.restore.status` as non-normative until the Gateway protocol owner approves a concrete API.
